key_insight: In retrospective evaluation, LabARIA coordinated laboratory surveillance agents and generated quality-control warnings before 96.4% of recorded laboratory actions.
clinical_relevance: Integrated monitoring could help laboratory teams identify specimen, workflow, and analytical quality issues for human review, though patient-care benefits remain unproven.
method: Combined multi-agent analysis of specimen workflows, internal quality control, and laboratory operations.
Selected patient-based real-time quality-control strategies across 35 analytes.
Presented tiered alerts and interactive summaries through a dashboard and chatbot.
evidence_signal: Single-center evaluation included 177,480 specimen-panel records and 75,103 internal quality-control measurements; warnings preceded 407 of 422 recorded actions, with a median lead time of 5.40 days.
watch_item: Retrospective action-based recall does not establish prospective usefulness or false-alert burden; operational forecasting also used controlled perturbations and synthetic staffing and inventory data.
paper_title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
